question: If 6x = 3y = 2z, then what is the value of (1)/(y)+(1)/(z)-(1)/(x)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate all parts to a constant **k**: 6x = 3y = 2z = k.

Express **bases** in terms of k: 6 = k¹/x, 3 = k¹/y, and 2 = k¹/z.

Use the mathematical relation: **6 = 3 × 2**.

Substitute k: k¹/x = k¹/y × k¹/z ⇒ k¹/x = k⁽¹/y ⁺ ¹/z⁾.

Comparing powers: 1/x = 1/y + 1/z ⇒ **1/y + 1/z − 1/x = 0**.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 6x = 3y = 2z

**Formula Used:** If am = b, then a = b¹/m; and am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61778689235d73c4449dad390b675e5ac57ebaeb02306e53c009c2173342be3f.png] 

⇒ Let 6x = 3y = 2z = k

⇒ 6 = k¹/x --- (i)

⇒ 3 = k¹/y --- (ii)

⇒ 2 = k¹/z --- (iii)

⇒ We know that 6 = 3 × 2

⇒ Substituting the values from (i), (ii), and (iii):

⇒ k¹/x = k¹/y × k¹/z

⇒ k¹/x = k⁽¹/y ⁺ ¹/z⁾

⇒ 1/x = 1/y + 1/z

⇒ 1/y + 1/z − 1/x = 0

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of Exponents

When multiplying two powers with the same base, add the exponents: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ.

Power Conversion

To isolate a base, move the exponent to the other side as its reciprocal: if xa = y, then x = y¹/a.

Equality of Bases

If am = aⁿ and a ≠ 1, 0, or −1, then the exponents must be equal: m = n.</p
